This Stealthy Box Trailer Hides a Luxury Tiny Home With Two Beds and Beautiful Styling
15 photos
Photo: Tilghman Trailers
While some people cringe at the idea of tiny living, others consider having a smaller living space a worthwhile trade-off, especially if that living space is mobile, as it would allow them to travel more, explore the outdoors, live more simply, and spend more time in nature. That is exactly what the XL adventure is designed to offer.
Larger and more commodious than a camper van, yet easier to tow and maneuver than a full-size RV, this box trailer conversion offers a comfortable little home on wheels with everything needed for off-grid living.
Built by Tilghman Trailers, the XL Adventure doesn’t pretend to replace a conventional house, nor does it try to squeeze all the features of a large motorhome into a tiny trailer. Instead, it combines a discreet exterior with an interior that has been transformed into a beautiful and comfortable living space that offers two beds, a full kitchen, an indoor shower, and the essential modern off-grid systems.
Tilghman Trailers was founded by Keon Tilghman, a man who built his first camper van in 2019 and headed to California to experience van life firsthand. He became passionate about turning small spaces into places that feel like home, and his passion only grew with mastery. Through YouTube tutorials and plenty of hands-on learning, he honed his building skills and founded Tilghman Trailers.
Photo: Tilghman Trailers Today, his company specializes in turning stealth cargo trailers into semi-custom tiny homes designed for adventure, with practical layouts, modern finishes, and handcrafted furniture. Customers can choose between two Tilghman Trailers models: the Classic and the XL.
As suggested by its name, the XL Adventure is the largest model of the two and is designed for traveling couples or small families. It boasts a dual-axle design and measures 18.9 feet (5.7 meters) in overall length, including the hitch, and 8 feet (2.4 meters) in width. It’s 9.4 feet (2.8 meters) high, and its estimated finished weight is approximately 5,000 pounds (2,267 kg), which means it can be safely towed by mid-size or larger SUVs and light-duty half-ton trucks.
One of the first things that some people might find appealing about this rig is its inconspicuous exterior. Finished in simple gray paint, the trailer might be a great option for those looking for a stealth build. Apart from a couple of windows, the entry door, and an awning on the campsite, there is little to suggest that this is more than a regular cargo trailer.
At the rear, owners can choose between traditional barn doors and a ramp, and the exterior color can also be changed to charcoal gray or white.
Photo: Tilghman Trailers The interior of the XL Adventure is only 14 feet (4.2 meters) long and 7 feet (2.1 meters) wide, but Keon got creative with the use of space. By using clever solutions like an elevator bed and hidden storage, he created a livable habitat with sleeping for four and all the essentials for life on the road.
There is no separation wall inside this trailer apart from the bathroom walls, and the living space feels like an open, studio apartment on wheels with a clean, nature-inspired palette of sage green, light gray, and warm wood tones. Baltic birch is used on the walls, LifeProof vinyl on the floors, and all the furniture is handcrafted.
Dimmable indirect lighting lets you create a nice ambiance in the evening, while the large doorway at the rear creates an open, luminous, and airy atmosphere during the day.
Photo: Tilghman Trailers The space is dominated by a comfortable modular sofa that faces an open-concept media wall with a large flat-screen TV framed by minimalistic wood shelving for books and decorations. It’s a multifunctional space for relaxation and other daily activities.
A compact kitchen occupies the front area of the trailer. It has both low and upper cabinets, which are paired with a 53-inch butcher block countertop integrating a stainless steel sink and an Empava induction cooktop. A large fridge-freezer is also included in its dedicated cabinet near the bathroom.
Speaking of the bathroom, considering the size of the trailer, don’t expect a full bath. It is a small wet bath finished with waterproof vinyl tile, which includes a shower, a small ledge for toiletries, and a dry-flush toilet.
But one of the most interesting elements of the design is the double-bed arrangement. The sofa pulls into a comfortable bed for two, and the builder added an elevator bed just above it, which is electrically operated and stays out of the way when it’s not needed. The upper bed is a standard queen size, while the lower one is even larger.
Photo: Tilghman Trailers For extended boondocking and off-grid trips, the XL Adventure trailer comes equipped with 600 watts of solar panels on a roof, a 600Ah lithium battery bank, and a 3,000W Victron MultiPlus inverter/charger that manages the electrical supply. A shore-power hookup is available. For your water needs, the trailer carries a 33-gallon fresh-water tank and a 30-gallon gray-water tank.
Other standard equipment includes a 7-gallon Basch water heater, 12V air conditioning, a diesel heater, leveling jacks, and a storage box mounted at the hitch.
Though the Tilghman XL Adventure can only be ordered with a fixed layout and the furniture design remains unchanged, owners can personalize the interior with their choice of finishes, including interior wall paint, flooring, furniture door-face finishes, and bathroom wall finishes.
Designed to appeal to travelers, nomads, and seasonal campers, the Tilghman XL Adventure box trailer offers a discreet and well-equipped mobile living space. Pricing starts at $70,000.

What the AI race is a contest over, and why the cheapest capable model may win
In part 1 of this series , I looked at where the US and China stand after two decades of investment. This installment asks the question the public debate tends to skip: when people say “winning the AI race,” what does winning mean?
There Is No Single Finish Line
The AI race gets described as though there were one finish line: one model, one moment when someone crosses first and the outcome is settled. The United States and China are not running toward the same point. If China is racing toward nine o’clock and the US toward two o’clock, both can run as fast as they possibly can and still not compete for the same prize. The useful question is what each side is trying to get, and what happens to the rest of the world once they get it.
Five Things Being Contested
One of ASML’s DUV machines. Image courtesy of ASML.
Frontier model capability. This is the headline contest: which model scores highest on the hardest benchmarks. The US leads, narrowly. Stanford’s 2026 AI Index put the gap between the leading US and Chinese models on the Arena leaderboard at about 2.7% as of March. In mid-October, the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index scored the best closed model at 58 and the best openly downloadable model at 46. The pattern is consistent: close on conversation, wider on hard reasoning and long autonomous tasks.
Chip manufacturing. The US holds a wide and, for now, structural lead: advanced chip fabrication sits in a small number of facilities the US and its allies control. Part of that lead is policy. The Institute for Progress estimates that with no H200 exports, the US would hold a 21 to 49 times advantage in AI compute produced in 2026, and that unrestricted exports of Nvidia ‘s H200 could cut it to roughly 1.2 to 6.7 times. Commerce approved about 10 Chinese buyers in May, but Reuters reported no deliveries as Beijing steered its companies toward Huawei . That substitution is not one for one. Huawei’s Ascend 910C trails the H200 in computing power and memory bandwidth, and Epoch AI estimates Huawei’s 2026 output at about 880,000 H100-equivalents against about 23 million for Nvidia, under 4%. The tightest constraint is high-bandwidth memory, which China cannot yet make in volume. Huawei is pushing anyway. In September it pulled its Ascend 960DT forward to early 2027, a chip Bernstein estimates will roughly match the H200 with more than twice its interconnect bandwidth, and said a 256,000-card cluster is being deployed. How large the US lead stays depends on Washington’s export decisions and China’s memory production as much as on chip design.
Research volume and open-source distribution. China leads here, and this may be the contest that decides what the rest of the world runs on. Chinese models accounted for about 41% of downloads on Hugging Face over the past year, ahead of US models, and the summer brought a run of Chinese releases: Moonshot ‘s Kimi K3, Alibaba ‘s Qwen3.8, DeepSeek V4.1-Flash, and models from Z.ai and Xiaomi . In October, Anthropic reported that Z.ai’s open-weight GLM-5.3 came close to its restricted Mythos Preview model on cyber-exploit tests, while NIST’s Center for AI Standards and Innovation put it about four months behind the US frontier. DeepSeek and Huawei have also released open tools for programming Huawei’s chips, aimed at reducing dependence on Nvidia’s CUDA software.
A note on terms. An open-weight model publishes its trained parameters, called weights, so anyone can download it, run it on their own hardware, and modify it. Many people call these open-source models, though the training data and code usually stay private. A closed model, such as those from OpenAI , Anthropic, and Google, can only be used through the company’s own service.
(gguy/Shutterstock)
The trade between the two is simple. Closed models are more capable, and open models are much cheaper. DeepSeek’s open-weight V4-Pro costs $0.66 per million input tokens and $1.98 per million output tokens off-peak (a token is about three-quarters of a word), against $5 and $25 for Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.7 and $5 and $30 for OpenAI’s GPT-5.5. That makes DeepSeek roughly 8 to 15 times cheaper. On SWE-bench Verified , a widely used test of fixing real software bugs, Opus 4.7 solves 87.6% of the problems; DeepSeek reports 80.6%, and an independent US government evaluation measured 74%. Put simply, the open model solves fewer of the hardest problems for about a tenth of the price.
Open models also reach what the best closed models could do only recently. Epoch AI puts the lag at about four months. So a buyer can pay a premium for the top of the range now, or give up some capability on the hardest tasks at a fraction of the cost and expect open models to reach today’s frontier within months. Many will take that trade for customer service, document processing, and routine coding, where the cheaper model already does the job. Open models are not only a Chinese story, either: hosting companies offer OpenAI’s open-weight gpt-oss-120b for well under a dollar per million tokens.
Capital. Stanford’s AI Index puts US AI investment in 2025 at about $286 billion against about $12 billion for China, roughly 23 times. China answers with state capital. Bloomberg reported in June that Beijing has drafted a five-year, roughly $295 billion plan for a national AI data-center grid, funded by state bonds, requiring at least 80%domestic technology and interconnected by 2028. That is about $59 billion a year, less than any one of the largest US cloud companies spends: Oracle , Microsoft , Amazon , Meta , and Alphabet together are expected to spend about $800 billion on capital projects in 2026, according to research by Columbia Business School’s Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh. The Chinese plan’s strength is coordination, bringing state debt, land, power allocation, and domestic chips together under one national grid.
Talent. This trend favors China and compounds over the longest horizon, which makes it the hardest to reverse quickly.
( miss.cabul/Shutterstock)
What the Summit Did and Did Not Settle
The most visible diplomacy of the fall was the Trump-Xi summit in Washington, which ended September 25. According to news reports of the readouts, it extended the trade truce to January 10, 2027, eased tariffs on about $30 billion of non-sensitive goods in each direction, and opened a dialogue on AI risks with a channel for AI-related incidents. Rare-earth talks will continue, and advanced chips did not feature. The leaders are expected to meet again at APEC in November and the G20 in Miami in December. The diplomacy is moving on its own track, and the competition in chips, models, and power is moving faster.
So What Does Winning Mean?
If you get to nine o’clock and I get to two o’clock, and we both got there as fast as we could, what did either of us win? People who study this closely suggest there may be no single winner in the sense the phrase implies. The more plausible outcome is an asymmetric split. The US likely keeps its lead in frontier capability and chip manufacturing, while China leads in research volume, open-source distribution, and the compounding effect of a much larger talent base.
Asymmetric does not mean inconsequential. One framing among analysts is that if China wins, it will look like procurement and not like conquest. It will look like a government IT office in Jakarta, Lagos, or São Paulo choosing the system that is good enough, priced aggressively, translated into the local language, and bundled with financing and support, the way much of the world ended up on Chinese telecom infrastructure over the past decade. Infrastructure adoption rarely announces itself. It accumulates one procurement decision at a time until the alternative is gone.
The stake, then, is a slow decision made country by country and company by company over the next decade about whose infrastructure the world’s economy runs on. Infrastructure carries the values, incentives, and leverage of whoever built it. A government or company that depends on another nation’s AI stack has handed that nation influence that is very hard to take back.
The Hugging Face Development
That split may not hold as cleanly as it appears. On September 3, Nvidia announced it will acquire Hugging Face, the platform where developers find, share, and run open-source AI models, for $12.93 billion, its second-largest deal after a roughly $20 billion asset and licensing agreement with Groq in December 2025. Hugging Face reportedly brings in about $150 million a year, so the price reflects strategic position more than earnings. Nvidia expects to close in the first half of 2027, pending regulatory approval, and Jensen Huang has said Hugging Face will remain open to the entire AI ecosystem, with no requirement to use Nvidia compute.
If it closes, it complicates the argument that China leads distribution. A US company at the center of open-source hosting, alongside the best available compute, would put American industry on both ends of the market: the frontier tier, and the distribution rails the inexpensive, everywhere tier runs on. Regulators will weigh chips and distribution under one roof. Nvidia’s last deal of comparable size, the $40 billion Arm acquisition, was abandoned in 2022 after regulators in several countries challenged it. Nvidia’s own filing lists the risk that regulators could bar Chinese models from the site, which could push Chinese developers toward domestic platforms such as Alibaba’s ModelScope and split open-source distribution in two.
The Commodity-Hardware Precedent
An earlier era of high-performance computing offers a useful precedent, and we lived it. Enterprise IT and supercomputing treat a processor in opposite ways. In a corporate data center, one hardened HPE or Dell server may carry hundreds of jobs, so it is built for reliability: high availability, N+1 redundancy, disaster recovery. Once it is stable, the team posts guards around it and touches it only for security upgrades, hoping nothing breaks. In a supercomputer, one processor may be one of a thousand working on a single job. In the CPU-cluster era, we built those machines from racks of inexpensive commodity servers, nicknamed pizza boxes for their thin, stackable shape, in place of a few exquisitely engineered machines from HP, Dell, Cray, or SGI. Each node was a worker. With proper checkpointing, if one got tired and sat down, the others picked up its work, and if one won the lottery and left for good, we sent it to the graveyard without much regret. It had already earned its keep by getting us to answers faster.
HPE Cray system installed at Stony Brook University
That allowed a different strategy: build the most capable supercomputer possible for the money. A lower price for a set amount of performance meant we could scale larger and reach answers sooner on the same budget. Once a system was running and producing answers, we started again immediately, hunting the next bottleneck in the network, cache, memory, compute, or parallel storage. Find it, break the system, fix it, get more performance for the price, then break it again, without stopping. At Gulfstream, that loop showed up as faster and more accurate engineering answers and quicker production, in a business where the goal is to fly higher and faster than anyone else.
The GPU and AI-chip world may be heading toward the same logic, which is why price-performance may end up a more decisive metric than peak benchmark performance. Huang said in May that GPUs Nvidia sold four or five years ago are now rising in price, and in August he described A100s, first shipped in 2020, as mission-capable through 2029. If durability and secondary-market value make older, cheaper compute economical for a large share of workloads, the same logic applies with more force to compute that was cheaper from day one.
This is also where the hallucination question resolves. A model does not need to match the best frontier model on its hardest tasks to be good enough. Its error rate needs to fall below what the specific workflow can tolerate. For a first-pass literature review, customer-service routing, or routine coding, many non-frontier models clear that bar at a fraction of the cost. For a cancer-treatment protocol or a nuclear engineering calculation, the bar stays far higher, and narrowly scoped domain-specific AI has the advantage over any general-purpose model. An AI trained only on vetted, authoritative nuclear engineering literature will hallucinate far less on nuclear questions than one trained on the entire internet, because the good source material is all it has to draw from. In naval nuclear power, an operator does not act on a single gauge he cannot cross-check against a second, independent indication. AI used for high-stakes work needs the same discipline: knowing where every answer came from and how much that source can be trusted.
The contest between general frontier capability and narrow, high-integrity domain capability will likely shape the next phase more than any single benchmark. It points toward specialized, verifiable agents built on clean, authoritative data and coordinated by higher-level agents, each layer improving the reliability of the one below it. That compounding is why neither country can afford to fall far behind. Once a system built this way starts improving its own tools and training data, the gap between leader and follower grows.
Part 3 covers the fronts running just behind the frontier-model race, robotics and physical AI and cybersecurity, and the engineering answers to the water, noise, and land concerns driving opposition to data centers.
About the Author: Larry Patterson works where high-performance computing, AI, and energy meet. A former Navy reactor operator aboard USS Enterprise (CVN-65), he founded and led Gulfstream Aerospace’s Scientific Research and Innovation SuperComputing Center from 2005 to 2020, where power, cooling, and cloud strategy were daily decisions. He has worked with the nuclear division of Continuum Dynamics. He is founder and CEO of HEAT Holdings, a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business developing patent-pending ways to finance nuclear power and AI compute together, with every source of data behind each deal rated for quality.

This Rossmonster Sprinter Is What Happens When You Design Your Dream Camper Van From Scratch
30 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / rossmonster
If you're set on what you'd like your dream camper van to look like, it's worth finding a company that can bring that specific vision to life. One company that specializes in adventure-ready homes on wheels that can work with custom requests is Rossmonster – today, I'm checking out its latest build.
What we have here is a conversion based on a 2024 Mercedes-Benz Sprinter 3500 with a 170" wheelbase. Its maker, Rossmonster, is a Longmont, Colorado-based company that specializes in turning trucks and vans into capable and comfy adventure machines.
This rig's customer drew his own floor plan, and most of what you'll see inside the van comes from that drawing. However, before we take a look inside the van, let's see what we can find on the outside. All it takes is a single glance at the rig to figure out that it's a camper van, with a variety of mods that reveal its "camper DNA."
For starters, it rides on standard Sprinter wheels but wrapped in all-terrain tires. Rossmonster took things up a notch when it comes to off-road capability by installing an Agile Offroad RIP suspension kit. It comes with custom-rate rear leaf springs, front struts, and upgraded front and rear shocks.
At the front, you'll come across a CAtuned bumper complete with a Warn winch and a bullbar holding two Baja Designs LP9 amber light pods.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / rossmonster On the opposite end, Rossmonster installed a Backwoods Adventure Mods bumper and three Owl Vans accessories: a spare tire carrier and a Sherpa carrier with an Expedition cargo box.
A ladder on the driver's side offers quick and easy access to the van's roof. There, you'll come across an Aluminess Weekender rack that holds two storage boxes, a flat-mounted Starlink antenna, solar panels, and a Fiamma Eagle awning.
Other notable mods are traction boards, awning-style windows, a Maxtrax table on the passenger side, a shore power hookup, and AMP Research powered side steps. Moreover, this Sprinter is designed to go the distance – what I mean is that Rossmonster replaced the stock fuel tank with a 45-gallon (170-liter) one.
Stepping inside, you'll be greeted by a warm, welcoming interior. Regarding aesthetics, the customer opted for cherry wood cabinetry, cream-colored wall panels, and Chilewich woven vinyl flooring. The look is complemented by cherry Lagun tables, a Paperstone Graphite solid surface countertop, and beautiful Pendleton cushion upholstery.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / rossmonster The interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. However, you can use a curtain to separate the two areas.
Rossmonster started the transformation in the cabin – it replaced the driver and passenger seats with Scheelmann Vario seats. They're mounted on swivel bases, so they can be turned around to face the back of the van. I have yet to test the Scheelmann seats, but every single builder says that they're much more comfortable than the stock Sprinter seat offerings.
Behind the driver's seat, you'll discover a large floor-to-ceiling unit with multiple adjustable shelves. Next to it, Rossmonster devised a bathroom hidden behind a striking cherry wood door. It boasts a Nature's Head composting toilet on top of a teak shower mat, a shower with a handheld wand, and some storage compartments.
Next, we have the kitchen on the passenger side. It features a dual-burner induction stovetop, a deep stainless steel sink with a cutting board cover and a pull-out faucet, a Nespresso coffee machine on a slide-out, and a 20-inch (51-centimeter) flip-up table that extends the available counter space.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / rossmonster An overhead cabinet, three large drawers, and two lower cabinets are available. The builders added extra storage compartments on the opposite side, next to the bathroom: a closet and three drawers. Another unit beside it houses a microwave oven and an Isotherm Cruise 195 fridge with a freezer compartment.
Finally, the rear part of the living space is reserved for sitting and sleeping. In the day setup, you'll find a large lounge comprising two benches, one on each side of the living space. They have custom armrests with integrated cup holders.
When you're ready to sleep, you can turn the lounge area into a bed. You must use the tabletop and a few extra panels to connect the benches and create a massive bed.
Above, you get two reading lights, a ceiling A/C unit, and a total of five huge cabinets that form a U shape. Moreover, a Van Essential roll-down screen lets you keep the doors open without having people peek inside.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / rossmonster The two benches hide the utility system. Power is on the left side - the electrical system's highlights are a 1,320 Ah lithium battery bank and a 3,000 W inverter. Three charging sources are available: solar power , shore power, and DC-DC charging while the engine is running.
As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 40-gallon (151-liter) freshwater tank, a 7-gallon (26-liter) greywater tank in the cabinet underneath the sink, and an outdoor shower connection.
Rossmonster thought of everything when it comes to utility systems. It added an Aqua-Hot 125D hydronic heating system that offers both heated air and hot water. You even get a backup in the form of a Webasto Air Evo 40 air heater that's tapped directly into the vehicle's fuel tank.
All in all, this fresh conversion by Rossmonster packs so much stuff that makes it as comfortable as a conventional home. The difference is that you can use this machine to go off-road and off-grid and explore the many wonders of the great outdoors.

source_document.body:
An electric truck at an iron ore mine in Australia. Credit: Rio Tinto.
Posted By: Cecilia Jamasmie October 30, 2026
Ageing mines and harder-to-process deposits are making production less predictable as financing and supply chain pressures mount, according to EY’s latest mining risk survey.
EY’s Top 10 Business Risks and Opportunities in Mining and Metals report ranks operational complexity as the sector’s leading risk for 2027, followed by capital, supply chains, rising costs and geopolitics. Companies should build more flexibility into investment and operating decisions as uncertainty persists, EY global mining and metals leader Paul Mitchell said.
“Mining has always been complex, but the degree of operational complexity is increasing as mines age and reserves are depleted and the new ones are more difficult to mine and process,” Mitchell said in a statement.
Regulatory compliance delays were the leading contributor to operational complexity, followed by variability in reserve grades, cited by 29% of respondents. Labour, material handling, processing capacity, transport and equipment reliability each concerned 24% to 26%. Depleting reserves leave operators with fewer mining areas, ore blends and processing options to absorb disruptions.
Selective investors
Capital remains available but investors are becoming more selective as commodity prices diverge. The survey found 44% of respondents were pursuing funding from equipment manufacturers, while 39% were seeking sovereign wealth funds and the same proportion were targeting government investment.
Supply chain disruptions are affecting mining inputs, processing, transport and access to markets. In response, 53% of respondents were investing in technology to improve supply chain visibility and 52% were increasing inventories or stockpiles. More expensive inputs and complex operations were also adding to cost pressures despite stronger prices for some commodities.
Government efforts to secure critical mineral supplies are creating financing opportunities while exposing companies to shifting policies and trade relationships. The survey found 28% of respondents anticipated direct government investment over the next 12 months.
Growing tensions
Cybersecurity entered the top 10 for 2027. Carbon, sustainability, changing business models and licence to operate rounded out the ranking, highlighting pressures that extend beyond replacing depleted deposits.
Mitchell cautioned that uncertainty would outlast near-term political events, including the United States midterm elections, and called on miners to reassess the assumptions behind their strategies, portfolios and capital decisions.
For critical minerals producers, the findings point to a growing tension between governments’ ambitions to secure mineral supplies and the industry’s ability to develop and operate increasingly challenging deposits.
“The important thing is not to wait for this uncertainty to disappear – it won’t,” Mitchell said. “Instead, mining companies must reassess the assumptions underpinning strategies, portfolios and capital decisions and build greater flexibility into how they operate.” Print

BYD is moving upmarket with its new flagship EV, featuring suicide doors, a gemstone grille, and possibly solid-state batteries.
BYD previews Yangwang Altior suicide doors and grille
Yangwang is like BMW’s Rolls-Royce and Mercedes-Maybach, sitting at the very top of BYD’s brand hierarchy.
The ultra-luxury brand offers BYD’s most high-end and technically advanced vehicles, including the U7 sedan, the U8, a hardcore off-road SUV, and the U9, an electric supercar.
Yangwang vehicles have previously debuted with BYD’s latest breakthrough tech, including its quad-motor e4 platform (delivering over 1,300 hp), its second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging, and its DiSus-X intelligent body control system.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Its next model will push further into the elite segment. After BYD revealed the name of its new flagship executive sedan earlier this week, the Yangwang Altior, the company has released several new details ahead of its official debut.
Yangwang general manager Hu Xiaoqing confirmed on Friday that the new Yangwang Altior will feature suicide doors, a first for a BYD model.
The new door design swings open nearly 90 degrees, Hu said, creating a dramatic, wide-open entrance.
Hu also posted a preview of the vehicle’s front fascia, complete with a dot-matrix Gemstrone grille and crystal-inspired headlights.
BYD has not confirmed many details, but the ultra-luxury sedan is expected to be about 5,500 mm (216″) in length.
Images of the disguised vehicle released last month show a similar shape and size to the Mercedes-Benz Maybach S-Class or Rolls-Royce Phantom.
HU said last week that the global launch of the new flagship sedan will take place in the UAE, not in BYD’s home market of China.
BYD has not revealed an official date, but according to CarNewsChina , citing “sources familiar with the project,” BYD aims to unveil the new flagship model in Dubai, UAE, around November 5.
The Yangwang Altrio will feature “unprecedented disruptive technology,” Zheng Yu, Yangwang’s executive general manager, said.
In one image, the vehicle was charging at a BYD Flash Charge station, suggesting it will use its Blade Battery 2.0 and 5-minute Flash Charging technology.
Yangwang flagship electric sedan at a BYD Flash Charger (Source: Zheng Yu)
Outside of the suicide doors, rumors suggest the flagship model will be BYD’s first vehicle to use solid-state batteries. Executive vice president Stella Li said during an interview with Carwow.es last month that BYD’s first vehicle to use solid-state batteries will debut in 2027.
The executive sedan is expected to debut around November 5. Prices are rumored to start in the 2 million yuan range, or about $300,000.
Yangwang’s current electric sedan, the U7, starts at 658,000 yuan ($98,000). The extended U8L, on the other hand, is the brand’s highest-priced mass-produced vehicle, starting at 1.45 million yuan ($217,000).

Ferrari Zero Electric Hypercar Concept Wants To Reinvent the Exotic EV Game – Rendering
13 photos
Photo: Instagram | paolomariagaravaglia
While McLaren , Lamborghini, and other exotic automakers are still deciding whether they should launch an electric vehicle or not, Ferrari has already stepped into this game.
The model in question is called the Luce, and it sparked a lot of controversy when it debuted earlier this year. It looks like a confused crossover, and some say that it shouldn’t wear the Prancing Horse logos on it, because it does not do justice to the brand. Others, however, definitely like the design, and they have gone as far as placing an order for one.
As you likely know, the Ferrari Luce is coming to the United States, and the first units will reach our shores in the second quarter of 2027. Pricing starts at $560,800, according to a recent report, and this makes it almost $120,000 more expensive than the Purosangue. And it’s up to every deep-pocketed individual to decide whether the Luce is worth that kind of money, or any sum, to be honest.
Now, the unveiling of the Luce has inspired some rendering artists to envision a proper hypercar from Ferrari. And by “some,” we mean @paolomariagaravaglia, who recently took to social media to present the vehicle shared above in the gallery. It is called the Ferrari Zero, and is an electric hypercar concept with “zero emissions” and “zero compromises,” according to its virtual maker.
Photo: Instagram | paolomariagaravaglia This thing does not look like anything on the road today. In fact, it could easily be mistaken for a sci-fi movie prop. To be honest, it also does not look like a Ferrari , but that does not mean that it is not on the exciting side of the segment. After all, it somewhat resembles a fighter jet for the road, and also sends some motorsport-inspired vibes.
The so-called Ferrari Zero may look like it has a canopy, and seating for one, a 1+1 (tandem) interior layout, but it actually features gullwing doors that open up to reveal a traditional supercar layout, with seating for the driver and passenger. The interior is only partially visible in these renderings, and combines black leather upholstery with some red accents for contrast.
This imagined machine has slim lights at the front, very aggressive air intakes, and an integrated apron that has been that has been split in half. We can see some air vents in front of the rear wheels, too, as well as extremely sharp-looking side skirts, and oversized wheel arches that almost reach the height of the car’s roof.
A wedge-shaped profile, a pair of slim taillights, a brake light integrated into the multi-fin diffuser, an intricate rear bumper, a rather clean rear deck, and a split-style rear window are also visible in these digital illustrations, alongside the aero wheels that have a five-spoke design. There are no traditional side windows and front windscreen, and this, alongside the extremely short stance, as well as the fat wheel arches, contribute to the vehicle’s unique nature.
Photo: Instagram | paolomariagaravaglia Something like this would need a serious amount of power in order to make a real statement in the electric exotic class, and would also need to be extremely fast, not only in a straight-line acceleration, but also on twisty roads, feasting on apexes at the racetrack like there’s no tomorrow. It would also need a more-than-decent range, and would obviously target petrolheads with really deep pockets, as it looks like something that would cost a few million dollars.
But could such a thing be in the making at Ferrari as we speak? That would be a no, because something like this is not even on the table. Nevertheless, if you still want a battery-electric Prancing Horse model, then you will have to settle for the Ferrari Luce, with its controversial exterior design, minimalist and modern-looking cockpit, and four-motor setup.
In case you forgot, the Ferrari Luce actually uses four motors, and these work together to deliver a total of 1,020 brake horsepower. This equals 1,035 metric horsepower and 772 kilowatts. A 122 kWh battery pack feeds electrons to the four-motor setup, and it can be charged at up to 350 kW. With the battery fully juiced up, you are looking at a range of 329 miles (530 km).
But what about the straight-line performance, you ask? Well, according to the model’s official spec sheet, you are looking at 2.5 seconds from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph), and a top speed of 193 mph (310 kph). Pricing starts at 550,000 euros (equal to around $625,000) overseas, and as we already told you, a little over $560,000 in the United States of America. Oh, and don’t let the quirky design tricky you into thinking that it doesn’t sell, because it does .
Now, before wrapping it up, we have to ask you what your take is on the rendered Ferrari Zero electric hypercar concept. Do you like it? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Paolo Maria Garavaglia (@paolomariagaravaglia)
